column1: # voice_allow.tsv — files whose first-person-plural words are DATA, not voice.
# guard/voice_check.py keeps the published prose first-person singular. A few files
# legitimately CONTAIN that vocabulary: a scanner built to detect appeals to consensus
# has to carry the phrases it detects, and its fixtures have to use them or the scanner
# would never be proved able to fire. Rewriting those would break the guard while leaving
# every test green, because the fixtures would have been rewritten to match it.
# Every line here is CHECKED. A file listed with no remaining matches is reported as a
# stale exemption, so this cannot quietly widen into a blanket permission.
# Format:  PATH<TAB>why the words in this file are data rather than voice
